It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii [[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]] [[ja:大御和神社]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Ohmiwa Shrine.jpeg | deity = all the deities of its province, [[Ōmononushi]]
[[Ōnamuchi]]
[[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]][[ja:大御和神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]][[ja:大御和神社]] [[sn:2]] [[sn:3]] [[sn:4]]
[[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]] [[ja:大御和神社]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Ohmiwa Shrine.jpeg | deity = all the deities of its province, [[Ōmononushi]]
[[Ōnamuchi]]
[[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Awa Shrine]] ** [[Susaki Shrine]] * {{ill|Hachiman Sōsha Ryo [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]] [[ja:大御和神社]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Ohmiwa Shrine.jpeg | deity = all the deities of its province, [[Ōmononushi]]
[[Ōnamuchi]]
[[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]][[ja:大御和神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]][[ja:大御和神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]][[ja:大御和神社]] [[Category:sn_crud|TEST2]] [[Category:sn_crud|TEST3]] [[Category:sn_crud|TEST4]]
[[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]] [[ja:大御和神社]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Ohmiwa Shrine.jpeg | deity = all the deities of its province, [[Ōmononushi]]
[[Ōnamuchi]]
[[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Awa Shrine]] ** [[Susaki Shrine]] * {{ill|Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine|ja|八幡総社両神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine|qq=|WD=Q135236158|1=Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine}} (other [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] of [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa [[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead [[co:commons:Category:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima]] [[ja:大御和神社]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Ohmiwa Shrine.jpeg | deity = all the deities of its province, [[Ōmononushi]]
[[Ōnamuchi]]
[[Sukunabikona]]
[[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii 2023.jpg|Enoshima Shrine File:Oomiwa 20230620 6.jpg|Other features == See Also == * {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} {{Shinto-stub}} ==See Also== * [[Ichinomiya]] * [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]] [[Ichinomiya]] ** [[Awa Shrine]] ** [[Susaki Shrine]] * {{ill|Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine|ja|八幡総社両神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine|qq=|WD=Q135236158|1=Hachiman Sōsha Ryo Shrine}} (other [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] of [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa [[Mount Miwa]] | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] |Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| name = Ōmiwa Shrine | image = [[File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Torii.jpg|270px|Ōmiwa Shrine]] | location = 644 Kokufuchō Fuchū, Tokushima City, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|34|04|10.8|N|134|28|46.6|E|region:JP-36|display=inline,title}} | type = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} (Small) / Former Prefectural Shrine | established = Unknown | structure = {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} | other_names = Kōnomiya (府中宮), In’yaku Daimyōjin | festival = October 19 (festival) }} {{ill|Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|lt=Omiwa Shrine|ja|大御和神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omiwa Shrine (Tokushima)|qq=}} (大御和神社) is a [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines all the [[kami]] of the shrines in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)|Awa]] [[Provinces of Japan|Province]]. '''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (大御和神社, Ōmiwa Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|WD=Q207309|lt=Tokushima City|1=Tokushima (city)}}, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately called "Kōnomiya" (府中宮). It is not to be confused with [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] which it is a [[branch shrine]] of Ichinomiya and Soja are not the same thing but were sometimes combinedhttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ {{nihongo|'''Sōja'''|総社|}} is a type of [[Shinto shrine]] where the ''[[kami]]'' of a region are grouped together into a single sanctuary. This "region" may refer to a ''[[shōen]]'', village or geographic area, but is more generally referred to a whole [[Provinces of Japan|province]]. The term is also occasionally called "'''sōsha'''". The ''sōja'' are usually located near the [[kokufu|provincial capital]] established in the [[Nara period]] under then ''[[ritsuryō]]'' system, and can either be a newly created shrine, or a designation for an existing shrine. The "sōja" can also be the "[[ichinomiya]]" of the province, which themselves are of great ritual importance.{{cite book |last1=Herbert |first1=Jean |title=Shinto:At the Fountain-head of Japan |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-59348-9 |page=105}} Whenever a new [[Kokushi (official)|kokushi]] was appointed by the central government to govern a province, it was necessary for him to visit all of the sanctuaries of his province in order to complete the rites necessary for ceremonial inauguration. Grouping the ''kami'' into one location near the capital of the province greatly facilitated this duty,{{cite book |last1=Bocking |first1=Brian |title=A Popular Dictionary of Shinto |date=2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1138979079}} The first mention of "sōja" appeared in the [[Heian period]], in the diary of Taira no Tokinori, dated March 9, 1099 in reference to the province of [[Inaba]]. {{cite book |last1=Hardacre |first1=Helen |title=Shinto: A History |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0190621711}} The name "Sōja" is also found in place names such as the city of [[Sōja, Okayama| Sōja]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]]. == History == The exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. It is said to have been established by {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement|1=Bunrei}}, with its deity brought from the {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}} in Yamato Province (modern-day Nara Prefecture). It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. The shrine was historically known as In’yaku Daimyōjin (印鑰大明神) and is believed to have served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|WD=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)|1=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}. Locals commonly refer to it as "Kōnomiya." In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}}, and in 1936 (Shōwa 11), it was elevated to the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226|1=Ken-sha}}. However, the "Guide to Scenic Spots in Awa Province (Revised Edition)" disputes the traditional story, stating that the association with the provincial governor's seal (印鑰) is fabricated and instead ties the name to the first of fifteen child deities of Benzaiten, called "In’yaku Dōji." == Enshrined deity == * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi no Mikoto]] (大己貴神) == Shrine Crest == * The shrine crest features crossed keys. == Sub-Shrines == Within the grounds, there are sub-shrines, including: * **Enoshima Shrine** * **Wakamiya Shrine** * **Inari Shrine** Additionally, the shrine oversees four detached precinct shrines. == Gallery == File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Shaden.jpg|main hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Haiden.jpg|Worship Hall File:Omiwa Shrine, Tokushima, Setsumatsusha Torii
